title: What does it cost a travel filming kit to also carry its footage backup?
summary: Chooses the capture kit (11,520 kits of capture-realkit, sourced devices) together with the lightest nightly-offload storage plan from capture-storage (microSD cards, two SSD copies of a 7-day trip, parallel readers, copy within 1 h) under one weight budget. Counting storage costs 3 of 18 shots at a 4 kg budget (18 become 15), and the lightest kit reaching all 18 shots grows from 3,900 g to 4,125 g (+225 g). Scaling bitrates from 0.25× to 1.5× moves that total between 4,025 and 4,300 g, and reader speed (90, 104, 312 MB/s) changes no shot count at any budget tried. Sweeping filming hours (2–8 h/day) and trip length (3–28 days) moves the lightest 18-shot total from 3,492 g to 5,307 g; within 4 kg only the 2 h/day kit keeps all 18 shots. Sourced: the action-camera bitrate, microSD mass, bus ceilings and the device catalogue. SSD and reader masses were checked against retailer listings (32–58 g per SSD, 28–85 g reader): the lightest 18-shot kit then weighs 4,040–4,262 g and 4 kg still reaches 15 shots. Not sourced: the 360-camera, phone and mirrorless bitrates (swept), and the laptop or hub the offload needs (not counted).
lede: what does it cost a travel filming kit to carry its footage backup? Counting storage costs 3 of 18 shots at 4 kg; the lightest kit reaching all 18 grows from 3,900 g to 4,125 g.
